subject: Temporary QPS lift for holiday promo - procurement checklist & pricing options
messages:
From: J. Sanders <j.sanders@brightcart.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Temporary QPS increase request for upcoming holiday promo

Hi Irene,

Quick note — BrightCart is planning a targeted promotional push for Black Friday week (expected traffic spike Nov 25-28). Our analytics team projects peak QPS could be ~3x our current steady state for short windows (predicted peaks of ~2,200 QPS for bursts lasting 8–12 hours).

We need options for a temporary QPS increase that:
- avoids hard throttling during the promo
- keeps cost predictable for Finance
- can be stood up within 10 business days

Can you please share:
1) Pricing options (pay-as-you-go surge vs. short-term committed burst pool) and the per-token surcharge assumptions;
2) Any minimum commitment or setup fees;
3) Procurement checklist — PO/SOW/DocuSign flow and expected sign-off lead times;
4) Whether you offer any one-off discounts for short-term committed burst windows.

I attached our traffic forecast CSV. If you can get a draft SOW or price band by EOD Tuesday that helps us route internally.

Thanks —
J. Sanders
Procurement
BrightCart Inc.
attachments: traffic_forecast_Q4.csv (CSV)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: J. Sanders <j.sanders@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QPS increase request for upcoming holiday promo

Hi Jason —

Thanks for the forecast, and timely heads-up. We can support the temporary lift and have two pragmatic paths depending on how BrightCart prefers to trade predictability vs marginal unit cost:

Option A — Short-term committed burst pool (recommended for predictability)
- Duration: choose 7 or 14 day window (we recommend 7 days around the promo).
- Provisioning: reserved burst capacity sized to your peak (e.g., 2,200 QPS peak).
- Pricing: blended per-token rate for the burst window (base hosted rate + burst surcharge). For a 7-day burst we typically apply a 15% surcharge on top of the standard per-token price, but we can discount per below.
- Billing: invoice at start of burst (prepay) with month-end true-up for actual consumption.

Option B — Pay-as-you-go surge (fastest to enable)
- No reservation; higher per-token surcharge applied in real-time (typically 25–40% depending on peak).
- Billed post-event; useful if you expect throughput to be highly uncertain.

Concessions we can consider for BrightCart: a one-time waiver of the setup fee for the committed burst and a discount on the burst surcharge for customers with an active committed plan.

Immediate asks from our side to prepare SOW/DocuSign:
- Final chosen burst window (start/end dates)
- Target peak QPS and estimated total tokens during window
- Whether you will issue a PO, and PO number if available
- Preferred billing contact and invoicing address

I attached a short procurement checklist to speed routing. Ben, can you confirm whether Finance can accept the proposed prepay + month-end true-up flow? Marissa — please review for account-level discount flexibility.

Next step: If BrightCart prefers Option A, I’ll draft a brief SOW and run a pricing concession to Marissa/Ben for sign-off.

Best,
Irene
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: temporary-lift-checklist.docx (DOCX)
From: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: G. Patel <g.patel@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QPS increase request for upcoming holiday promo

Irene —

Thanks, Option A (committed burst pool) is our preference for cost predictability. A few clarifying points from Procurement/Finance:

- Burst window: Nov 24 00:00 UTC through Nov 30 23:59 UTC (we'd like a small buffer before/after the core dates).
- Peak target: 2,200 QPS; estimated additional tokens: 1.7B during window.
- Discount request: can Redwood apply a 10% reduction to the listed burst surcharge? Our Finance team wants an upper bound on the per-token surcharge (a hard cap) so we can estimate worst-case spend.
- Contract/PO flow: we can issue a PO once the SOW and final pricing bands are confirmed.
- DocuSign: please provide an e-sign link and a concise SOW addendum; we'll aim to return the signed DocuSign + PO within 48 hours once economics are set.

If you can include both the prepay amount and the month-end true-up path in the SOW that will help us get internal sign-off quickly.

Appreciate it —
Jason Sanders
Procurement — BrightCart
attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: J. Sanders <j.sanders@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QPS increase request for upcoming holiday promo

Jason —

Appreciate the clarity and the window. Internal proposal and next steps below. (Quoting your key asks for context):
> Burst window: Nov 24 00:00 UTC through Nov 30 23:59 UTC
> Peak target: 2,200 QPS; additional tokens: 1.7B
> Discount request: 10% off burst surcharge and a hard cap on per-token surcharge

Internal notes / proposal:
- Commercial concession: we can offer a 7-day committed burst pool (Nov 24–30) at a blended burst surcharge with an 8% discount to our standard burst surcharge. We will waive the one-time provisioning/setup fee.
- Hard cap: we are comfortable providing a cap on the burst surcharge per token for the committed window (Ben — please confirm actual cap below).
- Billing flow: 50% prepay at SOW signature, remaining true-up invoiced at month-end based on actual consumption.
- DocuSign: I’ve prepared an SOW addendum and pricing sheet for signature (link below).

Ben — can you confirm the per-token cap we can guarantee for this window (I recommend keeping it conservative so legal/billing are comfortable). Also confirm billing code and whether Finance needs any further payment terms on the prepay.

Marissa — can we approve the 8% concession? If so I’ll send the DocuSign bundle to BrightCart and track for a 48-hour turnaround.

If BrightCart pushes for the full 10% we can escalate to a senior discount review, but this may add time to the approval. My ask is: approve 8% now to meet their procurement timeline and we can consider a retroactive credit if actual consumption reaches the top of their forecast band.

DocuSign / Attachments: SOW addendum + pricing proposal — https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/serve/BRIGHT-BURST-20261111
Attached to internal thread: SOW_burst_addendum.pdf, pricing-proposal-BC-20261111.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Ben confirms per-token cap and billing details
2) Marissa signs off on 8% concession
3) I send DocuSign to BrightCart with prepay invoice and SOW

Thanks team,
Irene
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: SOW_burst_addendum.pdf (PDF), pricing-proposal-BC-20261111.xlsx (XLSX)
